questions.question: During what circumstances can some Fundamental Rights be suspended, as per the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Fundamental Rights cannot be suspended under any circumstances
During any emergency, whether national or local
During external emergencies, such as war or external aggression

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**During external emergencies, such as war or external aggression**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **During external emergencies, such as war or external aggression**, some Fundamental Rights can be suspended as per the Indian Constitution.
 
• The suspension of Fundamental Rights is governed by **Article 359** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• During an emergency caused by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion, the President of India can declare a state of emergency, leading to the suspension of certain rights.
 
• Such a suspension is intended to ensure national security and public order during times of severe crisis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 359** allows for the suspension of the enforcement of Fundamental Rights during a declared emergency.
 
• The **44th Amendment Act of 1978** restricted the suspension of Fundamental Rights, ensuring that** Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during an emergency**.
 
• Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction for offences, and Article 21 guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty.
 
• The power to declare an emergency is vested in the President of India and requires parliamentary approval.
 
• The Indian Constitution has provisions for three types of emergencies: national emergency, state emergency, and financial emergency.

questions.question: Which of the following war/battle is associated with the hanging of Mangal Pandey?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Rebellion of 1857**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mangal Pandey** was a key figure in the events leading up to the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**.
 
• He was a sepoy (soldier) in the **34th Bengal Native Infantry regiment **of the British East India Company.
 
• Mangal Pandey is known for his **attack on British officers on 29 March 1857**, which is considered one of the first acts of rebellion against British rule in India.
 
• Following his actions, Mangal Pandey was arrested and subsequently hanged on 8 April 1857.
 
• The Indian Rebellion of 1857, also known as the** First War of Indian Independence**, was a major, but ultimately unsuccessful, uprising in India against the rule of the British East India Company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The rebellion began on 10 May 1857 in the town of **Meerut **and soon spread to other regions including **Delhi, Kanpur, and Lucknow**.
 
• The causes of the rebellion included widespread resentment against British economic policies, the annexation of Indian states, and the use of Indian soldiers to further British interests.
 
• The rebellion led to significant changes in British policies towards India, including the e**nd of the East India Company's rule and the establishment of direct control by the British Crown**.
 
• The events of 1857 are commemorated in India as a key moment in the struggle for independence from British rule.

questions.question: Bohag Bihu is also known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rangali Bihu**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rangali Bihu** is another name for **Bohag Bihu**, which marks the **beginning of the Assamese New Year**.
 
• It is one of the most important festivals in Assam and is celebrated with great enthusiasm and joy.
 
• Bohag Bihu falls in **mid-April** and is also known as the **Spring Festival**.
 
• It is a time for feasting, dancing, and singing, and it signifies the time of harvest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bohag Bihu is the first of the three Bihu festivals in Assam; the other two are **Kongali Bihu (Kati Bihu)** and **Magh Bihu (Bhogali Bihu)**.
 
• Each Bihu festival is associated with different agricultural activities and seasons.
 
• During Bohag Bihu, people wear traditional attire, prepare special dishes, and participate in cultural programs.
 
• Bihu dance and Bihu songs are integral parts of the celebration, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of Assam.

questions.question: The Second Five year Plan stressed rapid industrialization and the public sector. It was drafted and planned under the leadership of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P.C Mahalanobis**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **P.C Mahalanobis** was instrumental in drafting and planning the **Second Five Year Plan of India**.
 
• The Second Five Year Plan (**1956-1961**) focused on **rapid industrialization** and strengthening the public sector.
 
• This plan aimed to lay the foundation for a socialist pattern of society in India.
 
• It emphasized the development of heavy industries and aimed to reduce inequalities in income and wealth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **P.C Mahalanobis** was a renowned Indian statistician and the founder of the Indian Statistical Institute.
 
• He played a significant role in the development of India's statistical system and economic planning.
 
• Mahalanobis introduced the Mahalanobis distance, a measure used in statistics and data analysis.
 
• The Second Five Year Plan was part of India's planned economic development strategy, aimed at self-reliance and growth.
 
• The plan also emphasized the importance of science and technology in the country's development.

questions.question: The capital of the Mauryan empire was ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pataliputra**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pataliputra** was the **capital city of the Mauryan Empire**, one of the largest and most powerful empires in ancient India.
 
• The city was strategically located near the confluence of the Ganges, Gandak, and Son rivers, making it a significant hub for trade and commerce.
 
• Under the reign of Emperor **Ashoka**, Pataliputra became a major center for learning and culture, attracting scholars from different parts of the world.
 
• The city was well-fortified with massive walls and a moat, and it had numerous palaces, gardens, and public buildings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Mauryan Empire was founded by** Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE**, and it reached its zenith under the rule of Ashoka.
 
• Ashoka, after the** Kalinga War**, embraced **Buddhism **and made significant contributions to the spread of Buddhism across Asia.
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly organized, with a complex bureaucracy and a network of spies to maintain law and order.
 
• The **Arthashastra**, an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy, is attributed to **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, who was a key advisor to Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• The decline of the Mauryan Empire began after the death of Ashoka, leading to the rise of regional kingdoms in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**250**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **maximum strength** of the Rajya Sabha is **250 members**.
 
• Out of these, **238 members** are representatives of the States and Union territories, elected indirectly, and **12 members** are nominated by the President of India.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the **upper house** of the Parliament of India.
 
• It is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
• The Rajya Sabha represents the states and union territories of India.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ****Additional Information__**

 
• The **Rajya Sabha** was constituted for the first time on **3rd April 1952**.
 
• It is also known as the **Council of States**.
 
• The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The Rajya Sabha plays a crucial role in the **federal structure** of India by representing the interests of the states at the national level.
 
• Legislative proposals can originate in either house of Parliament, except for money bills, which must be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Rajya Sabha has special powers to protect the interests of the states against undue interference by the central government.

questions.question: The first and foremost role of ______ is that it acts as a medium of exchange.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Money**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Money** is primarily used as a **medium of exchange**.
 
• It facilitates transactions by eliminating the need for a barter system.
 
• Money serves as a unit of account, providing a **common measure of the value of goods and services**.
 
• It acts as a store of value, allowing individuals to save for future needs.
 
• Money also functions as a standard of** deferred payment, enabling credit transactions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of money has evolved over centuries from barter systems to modern-day digital currencies.
 
• Historically, commodities like gold and silver were used as money due to their intrinsic value.
 
• Modern economies use fiat money, which has value because the government maintains it and people have faith in its value.
 
• **Central banks regulate the supply of money **in the economy to control inflation and ensure economic stability.
 
• Money is crucial for the functioning of modern economies, influencing economic policies and decisions.
